g.text: Two tiers split by route: reads absorbed by cache, writes minting from an in-memory block
The read path has no join, no computation and no synchronous write. The analytics event is fired after the response is flushed.
add a millisecond to a redirect
CAS once per 100,000 links = about one write
every 30 seconds fleet-wide. Also gives tens of
minutes of write runway if it dies.
Reads target 99.99%, writes 99.9%. A link that already exists is worth more than a new one is to accept - so under pressure the
system sheds analytics first, then rejects creates, and never sheds redirects. Route-level tier splitting is what makes that possible.
